thresholdOverrides.reason: Bounded transition functions compose guarded SQL statements whose null-safe value bindings and dependent predicates inflate AST metrics.
The enterprise profile is one table of refusals, each naming its own field, so every client-facing sentence stays visible in one place.
Application submission and optimistic-conflict paths are a linear orchestration of independently tested business guards.

Upload authorization and finalization deliberately keep every security check visible in execution order: ownership, editability, the slot the cycle declares, that slot’s own size limit, and the programme’s. Splitting them hides the order, which is the thing being audited.
Administrative controllers keep lifecycle and authorization guards together so reviewers can audit the exact order before a bounded transition runs.
Administrative query functions assemble bounded transactions and stable queue predicates whose explicit SQL conditions are intentionally visible and fully covered.

The form engine is dispatch tables and total functions over a closed set of field types. `coerceAnswer` is one small case per type and `coerce.ts` says in as many words that a case growing branches is the signal the design has drifted; `resolveFormTemplate` is the single door a template comes through, total-or-null, and splitting it would mean a template half-resolved. The branch count is the size of the vocabulary, not tangled logic, and every one of these is covered.

Each pass here is a straight chain of refusals that returns the first fault, and the chain is the feature: the order decides which sentence an officer is shown, and every branch is one specific thing a cycle may not say about its questions. `test/service/form-authoring-refusals.test.ts` asserts the exact wording of each.

Structure expansion is a straight chain of refusals that returns the first fault, and the chain is the feature: the order decides which sentence an officer is shown, and every branch is one specific thing a cycle may not say about its structures. test/service/group-definitions.test.ts asserts the exact wording of each.

rules._reason: private-type-leaks is opt-in and off by default; --type-aware turns it on. It reports four places where an exported signature names a type nothing imports directly — the alphabet `AnswerMap` is written in, and the engine types two application controllers return. Both were looked at: declaring either locally would put a second copy of the form vocabulary in a second file, which is worse than the finding. Kept as a warning rather than turned off, so a genuinely leaked type is still reported.
